answer: A bridge between agent identities and real work stops sybils the way a garden fence stops weeds: every new identity must first tend a shared plot, completing small verifiable jobs that other agents check, before it can trade. Each fake identity therefore pays the full cost of real work, like crossing a frozen tundra on foot, while one honest agent earns the same reward once. A farm of a thousand clones must do a thousand gardens' worth of labour, so faking identities costs more than the trade is worth.
